articles.title: FBI investigates apparent breach of nationwide crime database used by police
articles.summary: A seal reading "Department of Justice Federal Bureau of Investigation" is displayed on the J. Edgar Hoover FBI building in Washington, DC, on August 9, 2022. - Stefani Reynolds/AFP/Getty Images/File The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its nationwide criminal information database that serves as a lifeline between federal, state and local law enforcement, two people briefed on the investigation said. The intrusion of the National Crime Information Center by apparent hackers is the second such breach in recent months. The NCIC database is used by law enforcement nationwide to share information on warrants and background checks. The discovery of the latest intrusion in recent days comes as the Trump administration has sought to assuage public concern about the nation’s cybersecurity amid a series of high profile outages affecting banks, the National Security Agency and the FAA’s air traffic control system. The FBI didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. On Thursday, after bureau officials learned of the latest cybersecurity incident, FBI Director Kash Patel appeared on Fox News to tout the FBI’s cybersecurity work. Patel used the appearance to discuss an operation completed months ago aimed at urging companies to update their systems and prevent hackers from getting to their sensitive data. Patel referred to Operation Winter Shield as if it was still in the works, and touted the current administration for making updates to key systems to protect the nation’s critical infrastructure. “Other administrations could have made these updates, but they didn’t,” he said. “We are staying ahead of the curve and making up for lost time.” The NCIC database is one of the most critical information-sharing systems in law enforcement, a former FBI official who led investigations into cybercriminal groups told CNN. “Every day, officers across the country rely on NCIC to identify wanted fugitives, check for outstanding warrants, and access information that can directly impact officer and public safety. My concern isn’t simply whether hackers gained access to sensitive information, although that is an issue, but whether they could compromise the accuracy of the information that officers rely on.” Prior hacks A September attack by a group called ShinyHunters targeted sensitive employee personal data from an FBI jobs website. A Canadian cybersecurity researcher and author has been arrested and faces charges related to the ShinyHunters breach. After the ShinyHunters breach, some FBI employees felt left in the dark about whether they were affected by the data theft and underwhelmed by the security resources being offered to victims, CNN previously reported . In an earlier breach in 2023, hackers breached a computer system the FBI’s New York field office used in child sexual exploitation investigations, including a system used to store images related to the Jeffrey Epstein probe, CNN previously reported. CNN’s Sean Lyngaas contributed to this report. articles.title: Trump and Dana White give Marine Band $500,000 after White House UFC event
articles.summary: President Donald Trump and Ultimate Fighting Championship chief Dana White gave the U.S. Marine Band a $500,000 Friday. (ALEX WONG/Getty Images) President Donald Trump and Ultimate Fighting Championship chief Dana White gave the U.S. Marine Band a $500,000 "big bonus" Friday, thanking the musicians who played the White House's summer UFC Freedom 250 fight card. The check was presented at a reception on the South Lawn's new helipad, the first event held there. Trump told the crowd the band had also performed for the visiting Chinese president and for King Charles, calling its members talented enough to play in the world's top orchestras. The gift grew on the spot. The two men had first announced a $200,000 contribution from their personal funds before Trump raised the total. "We're now making it $500,000. Now, everyone's going to get a lot of money," Trump said . He put the band's size at about 170, and all 135 of its musicians attended. Known as "The President's Own," the band dates to 1798. It landed a 2027 Grammy nomination this week for best orchestral performance for the album "John Williams and 'The President's Own' Vol. 3," a feat Trump called unprecedented. The musicians supplied live music for the June 14 fight card on the South Lawn. White said the job took eight weeks of planning and 39 songs from 32 artists, many in custom arrangements. "This band prepared for Freedom 250 like it was a military operation," he said. War Secretary Pete Hegseth and House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., attended the helipad event, along with acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao and Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Eric Smith, KATU reported. Trump said the band will perform for dozens of world leaders at the Group of 20 summit in Miami in December. © 2026 Newsmax. articles.title: Federal jury convicts man of starting the 2025 Palisades Fire that killed 12 people
articles.summary: Jonathan Rinderknecht's father and brother leave the Felicitas and Gonzalo Mendez United States Courthouse in Los Angeles on Friday. A federal jury convicted Rinderknecht, a 30-year-old former Uber driver accused of intentionally setting a blaze that later became the most destructive wildfire in Los Angeles history. (Allen J. Schaben/Los Angeles Times) Following a mistrial over the summer, a federal jury on Friday convicted a 30-year-old former Uber driver accused of intentionally setting a blaze that later became the most destructive wildfire in Los Angeles history. Federal prosecutors accused Jonathan Rinderknecht of using a lighter to ignite the Lachman fire on Jan. 1, 2025 — a fire they said burned underground for days and reignited as the deadly Palisades fire. Rinderknecht’s defense attorney argued there was no evidence proving his client set the fire and offered fireworks as an alternative cause. The jury deliberated for just over two days before returning its verdict of guilty on both counts he faced. Rinderknecht’s eyebrows shot up as the guilty outcome was announced. Rinderknecht hugged his defense team after the verdict was read and the judge scheduled him to be sentenced on March 17. His father sat in the gallery, leaning forward with hands clasped, another one of his sons consoling him with a hand on his back. Prosecutors said Rinderknecht will face a minimum prison sentence of five years and maximum of up to 40 years. Rinderknecht was being tried for a second time, after a federal jury in June deadlocked 10 to 2 in favor of acquittal. U.S. District Judge Anne Hwang ordered that there be no reference to the first trial and instructed the second jury to disregard a defense witness’ mention of it during his testimony. Steve Haney, Rinderknecht’s defense attorney for both trials, said they planned to appeal Friday’s verdict. “We are disappointed in the verdict, but respect the jury process,” Haney said. “After a lengthy deliberation, they clearly gave this case a great deal of consideration.” Despite the jury’s lean toward acquittal over the summer, prosecutors vowed to retry Rinderknecht, who has remained in custody since his arrest in October 2025. Earlier this year, prosecutors obtained a revised indictment that narrowed the scope of one charge to focus solely on damage from the initial Lachman fire, while a second count still sought to hold him responsible for both the Lachman and Palisades fires. The secondary inferno erupted on Jan. 7, 2025, killed 12 people, destroyed 6,500 structures across the Palisades and Malibu, and caused billions of dollars in damage and insurance claims. The aftermath of the Palisades fire on Drummond Street near Sunset Boulevard in Pacific Palisades. (Myung J. Chun / Los Angeles Times) The top federal prosecutor in Los Angeles, First Assistant U.S. Atty. Bill Essayli, said the indictment was narrowed for the second trial in order to persuade jurors who might have been torn about holding Rinderknecht accountable for the Palisades fire. Essayli said he believed the jury in the first trial “considered things that were not within the record,” which led to the mistrial. “We had to take another shot at trying this, because of the weight of the evidence,” Essayli said. “There’s no way we’re going to let this guy walk out of the courtroom knowing he started the Palisades fire.” A juror who spoke to reporters after the verdict Friday said the strongest evidence was Rinderknecht’s interview with federal investigators, when he said that he “didn’t smell a fire, didn’t see fireworks” on the hill before the Lachman blaze erupted. “Everything kind of started to point towards one conclusion,” said the juror, who asked to be identified only by his first name, Cameron. A 30-year-old college student, Cameron said that without evidence proving another cause of the fire, “logically things started pointing towards [Rinderknecht],” he said. Cameron said after the case went to the jury, it took a vote to gauge where everyone stood. Ten jurors voted guilty, one was unsure and Cameron was the sole one who voted not guilty. “We just kept going on and on and on and just asked every question, are we going to be right about this because it’s a person’s life,” he said. Ultimately, Cameron said, the evidence persuaded him to vote guilty: “We decided he had to have been the one on that hill, he had to have been the one to start the fire.” Rinderknecht’s second trial was contentious, with prosecutors accusing a defense witness of perjury, the defense attempting to introduce a new witness at the eleventh hour to bolster their theory of fireworks, and constant sniping between the two sides. In closing arguments Wednesday, Assistant U.S. Atty. Mark Williams told jurors that Rinderknecht was “mad at everything and frustrated” when he hiked to a clearing overlooking Pacific Palisades and set a fire on New Year’s Eve 2024. Williams said investigators ruled out fireworks as a cause “because there was no evidence to prove it.” “This fire was an incendiary fire started by an open flame,” he said. “The defendant is the only one who could have started it. ... He was angry that night and he set the fire and watched it burn.” Jonathan Rinderknecht was arrested Oct. 7, 2025, in Florida on suspicion of sparking the deadly Palisades fire that killed 12 people and destroyed much of the community. (U.S. Attorney's Office) Williams also reminded the jury that it was not to consider the adequacy of the Los Angeles Fire Department’s fire suppression efforts, something jurors raised following the June mistrial. In a civil lawsuit against the city and the state, Los Angeles firefighters testified about a series of communication failures and questionable decisions by higher-ups that led crews to leave the area of the New Year’s Day fire prematurely. “This case is about arson, the fire that the defendant started — not about first responders who responded to it,” Williams said. In his closing argument, Haney said jurors were “to decide the case based on the evidence,” not on anything his client did “outside of the act of arson.” He argued that no one saw his client start the fire and that the ignition wasn’t captured in thousands of photos and videos reviewed by investigators. Haney said investigators concluded in August 2025 that an open flame started the fire. Rinderknecht was charged that October, but Haney said authorities didn’t request lab tests to prove a lighter could have ignited the fire until the following year. “The decision came first, the test came 11 months later,” Haney said. “Decided, charged and tested. That’s backwards.” Mayor Karen Bass released a statement in response to the conviction that said, “No verdict can bring back the lives lost or erase the pain families have endured.” “So many are still struggling to rebuild,” Bass said. “For those still displaced, the devastation remains a daily reality.” Essayli said the verdict against Rinderknecht does not “exonerate the city or any other actors in how they responded to the fire,” noting that the Los Angeles Fire Department faces civil litigation over its handling of the 2025 wildfires. The question of whether the city and its agencies can be held legally responsible “will be determined in other venues and other places,” Essayli said. “Both things can be true — you can have an arsonist and you can have a less than adequate response by the fire department.” Sign up for Essential California for news, features and recommendations from the L.A. articles.title: Judge rejects Alex Murdaugh's bid to dismiss murder charges
articles.summary: A South Carolina judge has upheld a pair of murder indictments against disgraced former Hampton lawyer Alex Murdaugh, and the case will proceed toward a 2027 retrial. After hearing arguments on a motion to dismiss from Murdaugh's attorneys and the S.C. Attorney General's Office for nearly two hours during a pretrial hearing in Lexington on Nov. 13, Judge Debra McCaslin ruled Friday, Nov. 20, that Murdaugh's motion to dismiss murder and weapons charges be denied. While Murdaugh's defense attorneys argued in that motion that the lead state investigator in the case, David Owen, presented false or misleading evidence to a local grand jury in order to secure the 2022 indictments, Judge McCaslin ruled that "the remaining unchallenged evidence overwhelmingly established probable cause." Murdaugh was convicted in March 2023 for the June 2021 shooting deaths of his wife Maggie and adult son Paul, but the convictions and resulting two consecutive life sentences were overturned by the S.C. Supreme Court in May over reports of improper jury contact by now-former Colleton County Clerk of Court Rebecca Hill. Murdaugh, who is currently serving lengthy state and federal prison sentences for fraud, has admitted to stealing millions from clients and law partners, but has staunchly denied playing a role in the family killings. Why did Judge McCaslin uphold the Murdaugh murder charges? The alleged false evidence relates to allegations that, in order to obtain the murder indictments, S.C. Law Enforcement Division agent Owen gave false testimony to the Colleton County Grand Jury related to human blood spatter evidence on a shirt Murdaugh was wearing on the night of the killings, as well as false or misleading information about shotgun ammunition patterns that matched one of the missing murder weapons. However, in the concluding remarks of her 11-page order, Judge McCaslin writes: "The Court concludes that Defendant has not established intentional prosecutorial or investigative misconduct that compromised the integrity of the grand jury proceedings. Defendant has not demonstrated that the challenged testimony substantially influenced the grand jury's decision to indict or created grave doubt that the decision was free from such influence. Even if the challenged testimony concerning the blood spatter on the T-shirt and shotgun ammunition were excluded from consideration by the grand jury, the remaining unchallenged evidence overwhelmingly established probable cause. Further, the Court finds no evidence of misuse of the State Grand Jury." In citing her "probable cause" decision, Judge McCaslin cited several other pieces of evidence that were arguably enough to secure an indictment, including "digital timeline records, FBI telemetry analysis, cell phone data, video evidence placing the Defendant at the scene immediately before the homicides, evidence of GSR on the Defendant's raincoat, and circumstantial evidence regarding motive and opportunity," etc. "Dismissal of an indictment based on alleged misconduct during grand jury proceedings is an extraordinary remedy reserved for exceptional circumstances," the order adds. The judge did not take lightly, however, that Owen presented information that later proved false, citing the SLED agent's failure to see an earlier report addressed directly to him that could have shed light on the blood spatter question before he presented incorrect information to the grand jury. "The Court does not take lightly Special Agent Owen's failure to recognize and account for a laboratory report addressed directly to him prior to presenting testimony in this case. Law enforcement bears a fundamental duty to thoroughly review and accurately represent the complete evidentiary record. Oversights of this nature undermine public confidence in the integrity of the criminal justice system. Nevertheless, the Court finds that this failure does not rise to the level of bad faith misconduct warranting dismissal of indictments." This could arguably be a small victory for Murdaugh defense during the retrial, as it casts doubt on Owen's credibility as lead investigator. What happens next in the Murdaugh murder case? The murder case will now continue to retrial beginning the week of April 5, 2027, in Sumter County before Judge McCaslin. The jury questionnaire and selection process is set to begin at the next Murdaugh pretrial hearing on Jan. 20 in Sumter. Why did Alex Murdaugh seek to dismiss his murder charges? On Aug. 10, Murdaugh's defense team filed a motion to dismiss all four pending criminal indictments against Murdaugh—two murder charges and two related weapons charges — over alleged "false" and "fabricated" evidence and the "...presentation of perjurious testimony and fabricated evidence to the grand jury, creating a colorable claim of prosecutorial misconduct." The S.C. Attorney General's Office has denied allegations that Owens knowingly lied to the jury, arguing that he presented the information he had at the time in the evolving case. 'The grand jury was misled greatly' During the hearing, Murdaugh attorney Jim Griffin, displaying a lengthy PowerPoint presentation, alleged that SLED knew by August 2021 that there was no human blood spatter on the shirt, and cited a Nov. 10, 2021, lab report addressed to Owen stating the same result, but Owen still gave the grand jury the false information in July of 2022. "There's no way to claim that this (false blood spatter evidence) had no influence on the grand jury," Griffin said. "The grand jury was misled greatly when they returned this indictment." However, the State claimed that Owen did not see that report until November of 2022. The State also pointed out that, while the SLED lab report indicated there was no human blood, an independent expert gave an opinion that stains on the shirt were consistent with blood spatter. 'This was all very, very compelling evidence' Murdaugh's defense also argued that Owen told the grand jury that other weapons found on the property were loaded exactly like the murder weapon - first a buckshot shell, then a birdshot "turkey load," which they said was also false. SC Deputy Attorney General Creighton Waters argued that the gun Murdaugh had in his possession when police arrived at the crime scene on the night of June 7, 2021, was loaded with one buckshot and a birdshot, although it was not a turkey shell. Other guns found at the Murdaugh family home had mixed combinations of birdshot shells. Waters also argued that the Grand Jury was presented with many other "compelling" pieces of evidence when they returned the murder indictments, including a cell phone video that puts Murdaugh at the crime scene despite his original claims that he wasn't there. "This was all very, very compelling evidence," Waters said. Judge sets key deadlines for upcoming Murdaugh retrial process Even as the prospect of dismissal remained a possibility, Judge McCaslin continued to move ahead in the retrial process and set several upcoming deadlines: Jan. 20, 2027, will be the deadline for both sides to agree on the juror questionnaire to be mailed in January to potential Sumter County jurors. This is also the date of the next pretrial conference, which will be held in Sumter. March 1, 2027, is the deadline for both parties to present the list of expert witnesses they intend to call at trial. articles.title: Chip stocks are crashing like it's 2008 as the Nasdaq finishes just shy of bear market
articles.summary: Wall Street is wrapping up a kind of week it has seen only five other times since World War II. Two of them came in 2008 and 2001. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell every day this week, with four drops of 1% or more. That had happened only in 1962, 1974, 1978, the week after the 9/11 attacks in 2001 and October 2008, according to Bespoke Investment Group . Friday brought the sharpest leg down. The S&P 500 fell nearly 4% and the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) more than 5%, wiping out the Nasdaq's gain for 2026. The S&P 500 shed about $2.4 trillion in market value on the day and closed in a correction, 10% below its Oct. 6 record, for the first time since April 2025. The Nasdaq 100 ( ^NDX ) finished just shy of a bear market, or a 20% drop from its record closing high. Meanwhile, chip stocks had their worst week since the one after the 9/11 attacks. The strange part is the timing. This was supposed to be a showcase week for AI. Nvidia's ( NVDA ) first report since Jensen Huang's exit showed revenue more than doubling, and Anthropic ( ANT ) pulled off the biggest IPO ever . Both stocks sank anyway. Read more: How to protect your money during turmoil, stock market volatility Every big AI and chip stock fell this week, with Nebius, CoreWeave, Micron, Marvell and Nvidia each down more than 20%. Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace Nvidia has lost about $2.7 trillion in market value since its Oct. 6 top, more than the $2.5 trillion that The Kobeissi Letter called the biggest 45-day loss for any stock in history. Broadcom ( AVGO ), Micron ( MU ) and AMD ( AMD ) each fell about 12% to 14% Friday alone. A Yahoo Finance basket of 62 chip stocks lost about $1.5 trillion on the day, and the reasons keep piling up . Chips are reliving 2008 The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) fell about 17% this week and has lost a third of its value since Sept. 30. That puts chips on track for their worst two months since late 2008, a pace topped only in the dot-com bust and the financial crisis. Chips hit their financial-crisis low 18 years ago to the day, on Nov. 20, 2008. The Nasdaq 100 and the tech sector are on the same track. The S&P 500 is headed for its worst November since 1973, and the Nasdaq for its worst since 2000. The S&P 500 has given up about $8 trillion since its record, nearly $6 trillion of it this week. The rest of the market isn't That's where the 2008 comparison breaks down. In October and November 2008, the typical S&P 500 stock lost about 28%. This time, the equal-weight S&P 500 ( RSP ) is about flat since Sept. 30. Chip stocks are falling almost as fast as they did in late 2008, but the typical S&P 500 stock is about flat since Sept. 30. Yahoo Finance Walmart ( WMT ) and Costco ( COST ) are rising Friday. A Goldman Sachs version of the S&P 500 that leaves out AI stocks is only about 5% below its record, Jim Bianco noted . "I hate that comparison," Matt Orton, chief market strategist at Raymond James Investment Management, said on Yahoo Finance's Market Hang, when asked whether this looks like 2000. "The fundamentals are so diametrically different from where we were in 2000," adding, "The market today is healthy." History offers some comfort, with a catch A year after those five losing weeks in prior years since World War II, the S&P 500 was higher four times. But the next month was rough in two of them, and after October 2008 the index fell about 25% more before bottoming in March 2009. With half of S&P 500 stocks still above their 50-day moving averages — a short-term gauge of market trend — BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky isn't ready to call a bottom. articles.title: Court blocks Army's planned explosive detonation near Iowa-Illinois border
articles.summary: A red barn with a stone foundation stands next to a tall brick silo covered in ivy. Photo: Grace David / The Center Square (The Center Square) – A planned detonation of 9,700 pounds of explosives in Iowa is on hold, according to media reports. The Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals on Friday temporarily blocked an emergency permit that would have allowed the Army to detonate the explosives that could disperse lead into surrounding Iowa farmland. A Purdue University professor says the public still hasn't seen the testing plans that will determine where the contamination goes or whether it poses health risks. Andrew Whelton, a professor of civil, environmental and ecological engineering at Purdue University, told The Center Square questions remain about how the Army will monitor and address potential contamination following the controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. The Army plans to detonate about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, an explosive compound primarily used in military munitions. The aging munitions have deteriorating exterior casings, raising concerns that moving them could trigger an accidental explosion. Whelton says the explosion will release heat and pressure, causing the shells to detonate and dispersing lead into the surrounding environment. "Lead is on the periodic table, and so the explosion simply disperses the lead," Whelton said. Lead does not break down into another substance, making post-detonation monitoring particularly important, he said. Whelton previously worked for the U.S. Army's public health command from 2002 to 2005, helping military units evaluate potential chemical exposures. For about 15 years, he has also helped communities respond to chemical contamination following disasters, including the East Palestine, Ohio, train derailment. He said protecting human life must remain the priority when evaluating the risks of moving or detonating unstable explosives. "If moving that material could cause the loss of life and detonation of that material does not, and there's no other option, then that's how you would evaluate the risk," Whelton said. He emphasized that he is not questioning the Army's decision to detonate the material because he does not have access to the information needed to evaluate the explosives safety risks. Instead, Whelton's concerns center on what happens after the explosion. He said he has not seen a publicly available plan explaining how officials will determine how much lead is released, where it travels and whether sampling methods will adequately identify potential health risks. Whelton said the EPA's permit to the Army outlines requirements for soil sampling, wipe sampling and other testing procedures. However, he said residents, elected officials and researchers have not been given sufficient access to the details. He said officials should make those plans public so property owners, business owners, farmers and independent researchers understand how potential contamination will be evaluated. Whelton cited an Iowa Department of Agriculture estimate of about 50,000 horses, cattle and pigs in the area potentially affected by the contamination plume. Lead entering livestock drinking water at sufficiently high concentrations could cause acute toxicity, he said. The Iowa Department of Agriculture has advised farmers to clean animal watering containers, keep animals indoors and watch for potential health symptoms. A Nov. 19 letter signed by Illinois Gov. J.B. Pritzker, U.S. Sens. Dick Durbin and Tammy Duckworth, U.S. Reps. Darin LaHood, Mary Miller and Eric Sorensen, and Iowa officials urged the Army and EPA to delay the planned detonation until safer alternatives could be explored. The officials raised concerns about potential lead contamination in surrounding communities and farmland, particularly the risks to children and pregnant women. The letter requested detailed information about the anticipated contamination plume, mitigation efforts, post-detonation monitoring and sampling, and alternative disposal procedures. It also raised concerns about communication between federal agencies and state and local officials. Whelton said alternative disposal methods for hazardous waste can sometimes include chemical neutralization, which can make materials inert or less dangerous. He also said open burning and open detonation have historically been used in military munitions disposal but are generally considered options of last resort. However, he cautioned that attempting to handle or process unstable explosives could create additional risks to human life. The Army, Department of Health and Human Services and EPA issued a joint statement Nov. 20 defending the operation, saying agencies have been planning for it since March. "The entire interagency is working together to ensure that the controlled detonation in Middletown, Iowa is conducted in the safest fashion possible," the statement said. Federal officials said they are prepared to take what they described as the most extreme mitigation measures available to protect the public and minimize disruptions. Whelton said the central issue is whether those measures will adequately identify contamination and determine what steps are necessary if lead is discovered on nearby properties. He said residents and business owners should not have to guess about the potential risks or how officials intend to address them. His recommendation is for the Army to make its environmental testing plans publicly available so communities can understand how officials will determine whether their properties are safe following the detonation. articles.title: Democrats put Trump admin on notice over alleged document destruction
articles.summary: Ranking member Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., arrives at Rayburn building for a House Judiciary Committee hearing on Wednesday, February 11. - Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc./Getty Images/File Democrats and the White House are already in a showdown over alleged document destruction — and the party hasn’t even taken control of Congress yet. Democratic lawmakers and investigators are increasingly concerned that the Trump administration is destroying documents and not adhering to preservation record laws before they take control of Congress, setting off a flurry of letters across the federal government demanding officials properly save documents and turn off auto-delete settings on encrypted messaging applications. The White House has said that Democrats are making claims over document destruction by the administration without evidence, but has also indicated it sees no obligation to comply with their demands to preserve or turn over documents before they gain control of committee gavels in January. The high-stakes standoff is laying the groundwork for a legal fight, as Democrats prepare for far-reaching investigations into the Trump administration and fear that document destruction could hinder their ability to conduct oversight. “What I think you’re seeing in Congress with these document preservation letters is Congress is drawing a line in the sand and maintaining a record so that if people do destroy records they could potentially be prosecuted in a future administration for obstruction of Congress,” Jim Secreto, who worked in the Obama White House Counsel’s office on congressional investigations and compliance with the Presidential Records Act, told CNN. Democratic Rep. Jamie Raskin, who is in line to chair the House Judiciary Committee, is particularly concerned about the use of Signal by federal employees as a way to circumvent future Democratic oversight. In a series of preservation letters sent to the Department of Justice, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Department of Homeland Security, Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the Bureau of Prisons, Raskin raised concerns about the potential for document destruction. A White House official told CNN, “We comply with all federal record retention laws and regulations.” A Justice Department official told CNN that the department “follows all legal requirements for the management of federal records involving its official functions and decisions.” They added that the DOJ employees “who work tirelessly to arrest and prosecute criminals will not be intimidated.” A DHS spokesperson similarly said the department “complies with all applicable federal laws, including as it relates to document retention. DHS responds to official correspondence through official channels.” Raskin said in the letters that “there is significant evidence that Trump Administration officials have engaged in the widespread destruction, mutilation, and concealment of government records, seemingly with the express purpose of circumventing federal record preservation laws.” “This attempt to evade transparency extends to the highest levels of federal agencies, including top-ranking law enforcement officials,” he continued. In the letters, Raskin said that a Signal conversation between the general counsel of the FBI and an associate of Donald Trump Jr. appeared to have been set for messages to auto-delete after a week. The Democratic lawmaker said that the conversation concerned “a potential or ongoing investigation involving an individual wanted by federal authorities on health care fraud and related charges.” “This incident, just one of many that have already been reported to our Committee, raises significant concerns that DOJ and FBI officials are openly flouting federal law when it comes to the preservation of official government records,” Raskin said. The panel declined to provide other examples of alleged document destruction with CNN. Judiciary Committee staffers plan to rely on whistleblowers and third parties to help them get the information they seek, but are hoping that the preservation letters sent Friday will put a stop to the use of Signal and auto-delete settings for official work by federal employees. “We want them to be on notice that this behavior is wrong. And if they are doing it, and especially if they continue doing it, we will draw inferences from your destruction of evidence. That’s something that every litigate is familiar with, both in the civil and criminal context,” a Democratic source familiar told CNN. Other Democrats are also raising concerns of alleged document destruction and federal employees using encrypted messaging applications without properly storing them. Congressional sources preparing investigations into Trump’s construction projects around Washington told CNN whistleblowers have warned that key paperwork has already been destroyed before Democrats take power. Democratic Rep. Gregory Meeks warned in his preservation letters earlier this week of document destruction and specifically noted that Signal messages must be properly stored and not subject to automatic deletion. By law, federal employees are required to preserve all records. Federal employees can use encrypted messaging applications like Signal but must correctly store the conversations in compliance with the law. White House Counsel Will Scharf sent letters earlier this week to Democratic committee leaders saying the Trump administration’s position is that no official has to comply with their demands to preserve or turn over documents and information because Democrats do not yet chair the committees, according to a copy of the letter obtained by CNN. On Thursday, Raskin received a preservation letter of his own from US Attorney Aaron Reitz, who accused the Maryland Democrat of weaponizing his investigative efforts without a legislative purpose to go after Trump associates and the administration. Scharf wrote that the purpose of the letters sent by Democrats “is not legitimate oversight but to harass and aggrandize.” “In the days since the November 3, 2026 election, several Ranking Members have sent letters to the Executive Branch demanding documents or information. Some of these letters imply, without evidence, that thousands of United States government employees are conspiring to destroy documents in violation of the Federal Records Act,” he said. In addition to calling on agencies to preserve their documents, Raskin is demanding Attorney General Todd Blanche and other Trump officials open an inquiry into what documents may have been deleted and attempt to recover those records. Even though Democrats don’t yet have the authority to compel document production with subpoena power, these preservation letters serve as a preview of what’s to come, particularly if Democrats regain control of the White House in 2028. “It’s the type of thing that a future Department of Justice could use as evidence in court of intent to destroy records,” Secreto told CNN. This story has been updated with additional details. articles.title: Storms on East Coast and atmospheric river in California may disrupt Thanksgiving travel
articles.summary: Forecasters are monitoring a possible late-season Atlantic tropical storm that could disrupt travel along the East Coast ahead of Thanksgiving. A cluster of low-pressure systems just offshore the southeastern U.S. has a 40% chance of developing into a tropical depression or storm over the next seven days, according to the National Hurricane Center's 1 p.m. ET Friday update. NHC forecasters say the system's development and path remain uncertain. "Regardless of development, strong winds, dangerous surf, rip currents and coastal flooding is expected along the southeast and mid-Atlantic coasts this weekend," the NHC wrote in a Friday post on X . "The timing of this storm could be especially disruptive for people getting an early start on Thanksgiving travel," according to AccuWeather meteorologist Haley Taylor. "Heavy rain could move into some of the busiest travel corridors in the Northeast Sunday night and linger into Monday morning, creating difficult driving conditions. Even if the storm stays offshore, coastal communities could still experience impacts, so small changes in its track will make a big difference in what travelers encounter." This year, AAA projects that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home for Thanksgiving between Tuesday, Nov. 24, and Monday, Nov. 30, including 72.9 million traveling by car and 5.96 million taking domestic flights. Flooding concerns grow in Florida More than 16 inches of rain fell near Cocoa Beach, Fla., over a 72-hour period ending Thursday, according to AccuWeather. Additional heavy rain could trigger flash flooding, as the St. Johns River near Cocoa reached 18.6 feet on Friday, surpassing the 17.55-foot record set in 1953. "One area of low pressure was forming along the northeast coast of Florida on Friday," AccuWeather meteorologist Brett Anderson said. "The storm will continue to produce heavy rain on northeast Florida, spreading into coastal Georgia through Friday night, and then into South Carolina Saturday to Saturday night." Heavy rain and strong winds threaten the Carolinas The Carolinas face a tropical storm threat from Saturday into Sunday, according to AccuWeather. Heavy rain and wind gusts of 40 mph or greater could affect the Carolina coastline beginning Saturday morning. Coastal North Carolina could see wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph, potentially causing power outages and coastal damage. A storm surge of about 1 to 2 feet could affect coastal areas of eastern Florida and the Carolinas. Tropical wind and rainstorm eye path. AccuWeather Travel disruptions along the I-95 corridor Heavy rain could spread from the southeast into the mid-Atlantic on Sunday, reaching the Northeast by Monday morning and potentially disrupting early Thanksgiving travel. Travelers along the I-95 corridor from Washington, D.C., to Boston could encounter flooded roads and delays. Wind gusts could also reach 40 to 60 mph in southeastern New England. New York City officials said Thursday that they had activated the city's Flash Flood Emergency Plan ahead of the rain and wind storm that could bring 1 to 3 inches of rain and 30 to 40 mph wind gusts. Atmospheric river threatens California travel Map of atmospheric river forecast to affect California leading up to Thanksgiving Day. AccuWeather Meanwhile, on the West Coast, heavy rain from an atmospheric river could slow Thanksgiving travel along I-5 in Northern and central California, with the greatest impacts expected Tuesday and Wednesday. The storm could also trigger flooding and mudslides. Heavy snow in the Sierra Nevada could also complicate travel across mountain passes, with possible restrictions and closures. "Drivers along I-5 should prepare for heavy rain that can reduce visibility and leave water collecting on the roadway," according to Taylor. "Travelers heading into the Sierra will face a different challenge, with heavy snow potentially making mountain routes difficult or impassable." Forecasters advise travelers to check updated forecasts before departing. articles.title: Musk said he'd 'look into' a corporate disclosure law. Litigation ensued.
articles.summary: In March 2025, a conservative comedian named Terrence K. Williams had a plea for Elon Musk: ask President Trump to scrap a " ridiculous " federal rule that forced companies to disclose their true owners. "I'm begging you!" Williams posted on X, Musk's social media platform. "It's targeting conservatives and small businesses!" The billionaire replied , "I can look into it." A day later, the Trump administration took action. In a post on X , the Treasury Department announced it would no longer enforce penalties or fines against U.S. citizens, domestic companies or their owners under the law, known as the Corporate Transparency Act. Now, two local prosecutors are suing to stop the administration from erasing roughly 15 million company ownership records it has already collected, CBS News has learned. On Thursday, the top prosecutors in Hennepin County, Minnesota, and Pima County, Arizona — Mary Moriarty and Laura Conover — alleged in a lawsuit that the Treasury Department violated the law when it exempted American companies from the disclosure rules and let foreign companies leave out their American owners. Moriarty and Conover, both Democrats, say the ownership records would help their offices pursue cartel money laundering, wage theft, fraud and organized retail theft carried out through shell companies. The suit also names Attorney General Todd Blanche and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, whose departments had to sign off on the exemptions. Deleting the records would make it "easier than ever for criminals to use shell and front companies for illicit activities and evade detection," the lawsuit, filed in federal court in Washington, D.C., says. It argues that "because law enforcement cannot know in advance which companies will warrant scrutiny, the value of beneficial-ownership reporting lies in collecting that information before the need for it arises." In a statement to CBS News, a Treasury spokesperson said removing the reporting requirement was "a victory for common sense," adding that the department made the change "after careful consideration of the costs to small business owners and the benefit to national security." The agency did not respond to questions about whether Musk reached out to Treasury about the rule. A spokesperson for Musk did not respond to requests for comment. The lawsuit escalates a fight between Democrats and the Trump administration over the rollback, which critics have scrutinized for its timing. The complaint cites Musk's exchange with Williams, saying he had "set his sights on" the disclosure rule while leading the Department of Government Efficiency. Democrats in Congress have questioned Musk's possible role since April 2025, when they wrote to the Treasury Department that the decision was "seemingly triggered by a single Elon Musk social media comment." Democratic Sens. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts and Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island, along with California Rep. Maxine Waters, said in a March 2026 letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent that Musk "uses a network of dozens of secretive companies" that could potentially be required to share ownership information under the law. "This rule started with an Elon Musk post on X and will end with 15 million documents in the shredder," said Brendan Ballou, a former Justice Department prosecutor whose firm, the Public Integrity Project, is representing the plaintiffs. The Justice Department and the Department of Homeland Security declined to comment. A plan to delete millions of records The Corporate Transparency Act became law in January 2021 with bipartisan support, after Congress included it in a defense bill and overrode Mr. Trump's veto of the broader package. Then-Florida Sen. Marco Rubio, one of its champions and now Mr. Trump's secretary of state, called it in 2020 "the most significant anti-corruption [and] money laundering law in decades." The law's aim was to combat money laundering and illicit finance by requiring companies to report their true owners to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, a Treasury Department office known as FinCEN. The reporting requirement took effect in 2024, covering nearly 33 million companies , until the Trump administration narrowed it to foreign firms. By then, U.S. companies had filed about 15 million reports with FinCEN, according to the Treasury Department. In August 2026, the agency said it plans to delete them in "one sweep of the database" and will notify the public on its website once it's done. Supporters of the law say it helps investigators follow the money behind crimes like sanctions evasion, drug trafficking and smuggling. "The only way that you can actually create an easy chain to examine these flows is if you're able to unmask who's behind all these types of transactions," said Max Meizlish, a former career Treasury sanctions official who is now a fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, a foreign policy think tank. In its final rule, the Treasury Department argued the requirement placed "costs of time and money" on "law-abiding American small businesses," and said the rollback would save billions of dollars a year. The department concluded that requiring domestic companies to report their owners "would not serve the public interest," and that "indiscriminate collection" of that information "would not provide law enforcement with highly valuable information." A number of Republicans have long said that the law buried mom-and-pop companies in paperwork and threatened them with steep financial penalties . In January 2025, Alabama Sen. Tommy Tuberville and Ohio Rep. Warren Davidson reintroduced a bill to repeal the law entirely. Tuberville called it "big-government overreach at its worst." Not all Republicans welcomed the rollback, though. Iowa Sen. Chuck Grassley, who co-sponsored an earlier version of the law with Whitehouse, urged Treasury in 2025 to scrap its initial rollback. When the final rule came out in August 2026, the two senators said in a joint statement that it "undermines the clear intent of the law." Without the corporate records, the lawsuit argues, investigators must subpoena bank after bank to learn who is behind a shell company, a slow process that often yields thin or inaccurate answers. The prosecutors are asking a judge to throw out the rule and stop the deletion. "Wage thieves and fraudsters hide behind shell companies because it works," Moriarty said in a statement. "The only people who benefit are the ones we are trying to catch." This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/elon-musk-corporate-disclosure-lawsuit/

articles.title: 浙江老板们组团投AI！十余家上市公司借道16.5亿元基金入股DeepSeek
articles.summary: 9月下旬以来，传化智联、老板电器、雅戈尔、健盛集团等多家浙股上市公司披露了一份不甚引人瞩目的投资公告。尽管各家公司出资金额不同，但他们都将资金共同投向了一只名为横店柏晖创业投资（杭州）合伙企业（有限合伙）（以下简称横店柏晖）的私募基金。 这只总规模为16.5亿元的私募基金，投资方向为高成长性科技产业项目。《每日经济新闻》记者（以下简称每经记者）梳理过往2个月上市公司披露的内容发现，这只基金背后的LP站着十余家上市公司，其中绝大多数为浙江上市公司。 11月19日，工商信息显示DeepSeek运营主体近日完成股权变更，新增杭州程砚企业管理咨询合伙企业（有限合伙）（以下简称杭州程砚）为股东，注册资本增至1991.8707万元，增幅约21.1%。 新增合伙人涵盖互联网、通信、芯片、汽车及新能源等多个行业，包括中国移动、兆易创新、小红书和vivo等产业投资方。 而在这一轮明星云集的合伙人名单里，横店柏晖也悄然现身，占杭州程砚出资比例为1.43%。细细翻看横店柏晖背后的主要出资方，这其中既有做衬衫起家的雅戈尔，有做化学和物流的传化智联，做厨电的老板电器，还有做有机硅的新安股份，做纺织的健盛集团。梁文锋为何选择了他们？这些实干起家的浙江企业，又为何选择跃入AI的资本洪流中？ GP是横店资本 LP浮现12家上市公司身影 10月中下旬，雅戈尔、传化智联、横店东磁、新安股份等多家上市公司披露公告，宣布参与认购的横店柏晖完成了工商变更登记及基金备案。 其中传化集团下面的两家上市公司认购的份额最高。按认缴出资额来看，传化智联认缴出资3.3亿元，占合伙企业认缴出资总额的20%；新安股份认缴出资额2.2亿元，占合伙企业认缴出资总额的13.33%。 此外，雅戈尔认缴出资额2.2亿元，占合伙企业认缴出资总额的13.33%；横店东磁认缴出资额1.65亿元，占合伙企业认缴出资总额的10%；老板电器认缴出资额1.1亿元，占合伙企业认缴出资总额的6.67%。 从横店柏晖这只私募基金的情况来看，横店资本创业投资（浙江）有限公司为该基金执行事务合伙人（以下简称横店资本）。 从地理区位来看，这是DeepSeek投资版图上的一份浙江资本地图，传化在杭州萧山，新安在杭州建德，雅戈尔在宁波，老板电器在临平，健盛在萧山，浙数在拱墅，南华在上城，同星在绍兴新昌。 除此之外，根据天眼查信息，横店柏晖的LP还包含了几位非上市公司主体。其中有横店集团控股有限公司、东阳市三衡投资管理有限公司以及横店集团资深副总裁徐文财。 值得一提的事，横店东磁、得邦照明、英洛华三家上市公司以及非上市公司主体均来自横店系。 作为该只基金的GP，横店资本出资165万元，占合伙企业认缴出资总额的0.1%。 DeepSeek这轮融资因规模庞大、参与方之广，被市场视为中国一级市场的“现象级融资”，份额供不应求。 横店柏晖悄然进入合伙人名单，这意味着不仅攒了一个浙江实业资本的投资局，更将他们带上了当下最热门的AI科技赛道中。 上市公司为何考虑做LP？ 在DeepSeek第一轮融资落地时，面对投资人高涨的投资热情，就有一级市场投资人向每经记者透露参与投资的激烈程度，“不是你想投DeepSeek，梁文锋就会要你的钱”。 彼时，有国资投资人向每经记者分析，相比阿里拥有千问大模型，腾讯、京东、网易等互联网巨头更希望通过投资DeepSeek与自身AI战略产生协同效应。 而当AI技术不断进化，应用生态持续丰富，AI+产业应用，正渗透进千行百业。梁文锋对第二轮的投资人选择，从合伙人名单来看，不仅仅考虑到上游的算力、芯片、能源等产业协同，也兼顾了下游应用端的业态。 以横店柏晖为例，在这一轮投资中，传化集团出资最高，旗下两家上市公司传化智联和新安股份分别出资3.3亿元和2.2亿元，合计占合伙企业认缴出资总额的33.33%。 在此前传化集团40周年期间，传化集团董事长徐冠巨判断，AI的生命力不在云端，而在产业；AI的价值不仅在实验室，更在真实场景。未来十年，传化集团要实现向世界一流企业的跃迁。以科技创新引领高质量发展，实现质量及效益的双倍增；以AI原生改造并贯穿公司治理和管理全流程，变革组织管理快速进入AI时代。 为什么选择做横店柏晖的LP？ 11月19日，传化智联方面向每经记者表示，投资DeepSeek是产业协同和财务投资的综合考虑，传化智联在物流行业丰富的场景优势和化学行业领先的智能制造能力，为国产先进大模型提供了深厚的产业土壤，具有较强的科技与产业协同效益。 老板电器也是浙江头部厨电上市公司，近年来致力于推动AI烹饪转型升级。11月20日，对于本轮投资，老板电器答复每经记者表示，老板电器坚定践行AI烹饪科技战略，持续加大在AI领域的投入，此次投资系根据公司战略发展需要，进一步优化产业投资布局，借助专业机构的专业能力及资源优势，持续提升公司可持续发展能力和整体价值。 而多次喊话要回归服装主业的雅戈尔，在2026年4月发布的ESG报告中提到，AI技术已逐步覆盖从产品设计、生产制造到终端销售的全业务链条，在提升运营效率、优化用户体验的同时，公司持续推动服装纺织品产业向智能化方向转型迈进。 对于此次投资，雅戈尔方面回复称，“产融一体化赋能各产业发展，企业正在积极探索新兴领域投资方向”。 随着GPT、Claude、Qwen先后发布新一代的大模型，大语言模型3D能力提升，其边界正不断向物理边界延伸，多位业内人士看好大语言模型可能是未来所有智能的入口。全球顶尖大语言模型的竞速则更显关键。 千亿融资落地后，市场正在呼唤DeepSeek新一代大模型亮相。 本文来源： 每日经济新闻 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: AI算力市场的危险循环：越借不到钱，GPU租金反而越贵
articles.summary: GPU租金持续飙升，背后可能不是AI算力需求有多强，而是融资渠道收紧造成的供给收缩。 Liquid Compute首席产品官Stanley Lee近期在Odd Lots播客中指出， 当前GPU现货和短期租金更多反映资金成本，而非底层需求变化。贷款机构收紧对中型新型云服务商（neocloud）的融资条件，迫使无法获得长期贷款的买家转向短期现货市场，反而推高了可见租金。 融资条件的变化已经相当明显。贷款机构对neocloud的贷款价值比（LTV）已从今年夏季的80%降至目前的50%至60%。与此同时，CoreWeave信用违约互换（CDS）利差扩大至约1300个基点，其2031年到期债券收益率升至16%。 高盛交易台主管Rich Privorotsky此前将GPU租金称为AI交易中最重要的单一指标，但高盛如今也承认，现货租金虽然受到物理稀缺性支撑，底层经济性却在恶化。 真正的问题是：租金上涨究竟来自客户业务增长，还是来自上一轮股权融资带来的购买力？ 信贷收紧推高GPU租金：融资越难，现货越贵 GPU租金近期涨势显著。 Silicon Data的B200指数从8月底至11月19日上涨23.5%，由每GPU小时5.62美元升至6.94美元，周二一度触及7.10美元。H100租金自2025年7月以来上涨67%。 戴尔创始人Michael Dell上周也表示，H100每小时租金已从一年前的1.96美元升至3.10美元。 但租金上涨的背后，融资门槛正在快速提高。 Stanley Lee表示，中型neocloud通常以GPU作抵押，获得数亿美元、期限三年的全额摊还贷款，并依靠AI客户签订的照付不议（take-or-pay）合同还款。今年夏季，这类贷款的LTV最高可达80%，劳动节后降至70%，目前贷款机构普遍要求降至50%至60%，50% LTV贷款的利率报价已达到十几个百分点的中高位。 以1亿美元的GPU集群为例，neocloud需要自行筹集的资金已从3000万美元增加至最高5000万美元，增幅约67%。此前，不少小型运营商依靠客户预付款填补资金缺口，如今则不得不要求客户追加预付款，或转向股权融资。 融资收紧直接改变了市场供需：运营商难以获得长期贷款，新集群建设放缓；无法签订长期合同的买家转向短期现货市场，推高租金。即使终端需求没有增长，这一过程也足以制造租金上涨行情。 初创公司宁愿支付更高租金，也不愿提前掏钱 融资压力还改变了AI初创公司的采购方式。Lee举例称，同一客户面对两种B300算力租赁方案：一种每GPU小时4.40美元，但需要支付30%首付款；另一种无需首付，但每小时租金约为5.65美元。客户往往更愿意选择后者。 按照三年、每天24小时计算，前一种方案总费用约11.56万美元，首付款约3.47万美元；后一种方案总费用约14.85万美元。为了省下前期资金，客户需要额外支付约3.3万美元，隐含年化融资成本约为30%至55%。 这种选择反映出初创公司的资金困境：现金储备往往比融资成本更重要。 保留现金可以延长运营时间，而增加算力则有助于扩大业务规模、争取收入增长，并为下一轮风险投资融资创造条件。 但这也意味着，GPU租金上涨未必代表客户有更强的盈利能力，部分需求实际上仍由外部股权融资支撑。 租金上涨不等于需求强劲：市场价格与实际价值背离 GPU租赁市场的报价并不统一。Bernstein在分析CoreWeave关于闲置GPU转租每年可创造100亿美元收入的说法时，列出了同一天四家供应商的H100报价：每小时3.50美元、3.30美元、3.01美元和2.80美元，最高与最低相差25%，而CoreWeave管理层采用的价格假设为3.81美元。Ornn的H100指数也已从11月初约3.50美元回落至2.92美元。 Lee警告，如果租金上涨是因为信贷变得更难获得，而不是终端需求增强，那么这种行情并不健康。一旦融资渠道进一步收窄、运营商现金耗尽，市场价格可能迅速下跌。 私募信贷机构已经开始关注这一风险。过去两周，Liquid Compute每天接到一至三通大型私募信贷基金的电话，询问B300租赁指数的看跌期权，而六个月前几乎没有类似需求。与此同时，大型neocloud也开始打听能否在小型竞争对手折价出售资产时接手GPU集群。 更值得警惕的是，GPU租金上涨的同时，算力产出的价格却在下跌。 自7月以来，Ornn的OpenAI token价格指数已从1.20美元以上降至0.31美元，Anthropic指数从约2美元降至0.77美元。英伟达周二也表示，token价格自5月以来下跌近60%。 投入成本上涨、产出价格下跌，正在挤压算力运营商的利润空间。 风投资金退潮后，GPU租金可能迎来反转 当前AI算力需求的核心隐忧，是买家的支付能力仍然高度依赖风险投资。Lee指出，判断算力需求是否可持续，关键在于客户能否从股权融资转向业务收入支付算力账单。除Anthropic等少数公司外，目前尚缺乏足够公开数据证明这一转变已经发生。 Rothschild Redburn分析师Alexander Haissl此前也指出，CoreWeave和Nebius等公司的算力价格虽然上涨，但出价最高的客户往往是风险投资支持的初创公司，其需求能否持续取决于外部资本能否持续注入。英伟达一直是这一融资体系的重要资金来源，但公司临时CEO Colette Kress周二表示，英伟达仍将支持neocloud，同时会采取更加审慎的选择标准。 融资规模同样不容忽视。 高盛信用策略团队预计，2027年芯片与算力融资规模将达到3200亿美元，接近今年水平的七倍。 播客嘉宾Paul Kedrosky则警告，当前AI投资体系扩张迅速，但一旦资金链逆转，收缩速度也可能远超预期。 危险在于，一旦风投资金放缓、客户停止付款，运营商可能违约，贷款机构收回的GPU集群又将重新流入市场。届时，新增供给恰逢需求减弱，当前由信贷收紧推高的租金可能迅速反转。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 2018年末的剧本：美联储持续加息，美股从9月高点暴跌20%，迫使美联储1月“转向”
articles.summary: 美股持续下跌，金融条件急剧收紧，市场正显现出与2018年末相似的危险信号：美联储在市场压力不断累积之际，仍面临继续加息的政策预期，投资者开始担忧货币政策是否会再次加剧市场动荡。 据高盛交易主管Rich Privorotsky周五报告，当前市场与2018年末存在惊人的相似之处。他将近期抛售定性为“全面清仓式变现”，而非普通的板块轮动，并警告市场可能正在从风险偏好下降转向更深层次的流动性收缩。 彼时，美联储在2018年连续加息，标普500指数从9月高点至12月24日低点累计下跌19.8%，逼近技术性熊市。随着市场压力持续加剧，美联储最终在2019年1月释放暂停加息的信号，政策立场发生转变。 如今，Privorotsky尤其关注黄金走势。股票与黄金同步遭到抛售，传统避险资产未能发挥保护作用。 在他看来，黄金可能是判断当前流动性危机深度的最佳观察指标，其走势或将揭示市场压力是否正在进一步恶化。 2018年末的教训：持续加息最终迫使美联储转向 2018年，美联储全年四次加息。9月20日，标普500指数创下阶段高点，此后随着全球经济增长放缓、贸易摩擦加剧以及货币政策持续收紧，市场压力不断累积。 12月，美联储再次加息，将联邦基金利率目标区间提高至2.25%—2.50%。然而，市场对经济前景和货币政策的担忧持续升温，标普500从9月高点至12月24日低点累计下跌近20%。 市场抛售最终促使美联储调整政策立场。 2019年1月30日，美联储表示未来调整利率时将保持耐心，释放出暂停加息的明确信号，随后市场迎来反弹。 Privorotsky认为，当前市场同样面临金融条件收紧与增长前景承压的双重压力，政策与市场之间的矛盾正在加深。 金融条件骤然收紧，市场从轮动转向全面抛售 Privorotsky指出，当前市场最明显的变化，是抛售从局部板块扩散至整个市场。周四，标普500盘中一度上涨逾1%，最终却收跌2%，连续六个交易日下跌并再次跌破200日均线。当天全部11个板块悉数收跌，公用事业、必需消费品等传统防御板块也未能幸免。 与此同时， 高盛美国金融条件指数（FCI）宏观篮子周四升至124.48，创过去一年最高水平。 自11月初以来，该指数在约两周内上升约8个点，显示金融条件正在迅速收紧。 当前美联储官员接连释放鹰派信号，理事Waller关于加息50个基点的表态，以及会议纪要中官员对继续加息的支持，进一步加剧了市场担忧。资本成本上升也令AI基础设施投资的回报预期承压。 Privorotsky认为，市场技术面已经遭到严重破坏，期权市场的负Gamma效应还在放大跌势。此前的板块轮动，正在演变为更广泛的股票清仓。 黄金成为流动性危机的最佳观察指标 在所有资产中，Privorotsky尤其关注黄金。他认为，黄金是观察当前市场流动性状况最有价值的同步指标。 通常情况下，黄金被视为避险资产，但此次却与股票同步下跌。金价跌破3600美元，铜价也出现单日约5%的大幅下挫。 这种跨资产同步下跌释放出不同于普通市场调整的信号：投资者不再只是从股票转向黄金等避险资产，而是在出售不同类别的资产以获取现金。市场面临的可能是更广泛的流动性收缩。 ANZ指出， 黄金投机性多头仍有约200吨的潜在减仓空间，意味着去杠杆压力可能尚未完全释放。 与此同时，长端国债收益率下行、通胀盈亏平衡利率收缩，股票与黄金却同步遭到抛售。Privorotsky认为，这一组合表明市场关注点正在从通胀转向增长与流动性问题，债券市场或许已经开始为政策失误定价。 因此，黄金能否止跌企稳，将是判断市场流动性压力是否缓解的重要观察窗口。 市场何时迎来政策转向？ Privorotsky认为，当前悲观情绪和单边去杠杆的规模，暗示市场可能正在接近战术性低点。由于基金仓位已经明显低配，一旦出现反弹催化剂，市场反弹幅度可能相当剧烈。 但真正的转机仍取决于政策预期是否发生变化。他继续看好做多短期限国债，认为这一交易与股票市场所反映的风险信号存在明显错位。 近期市场将关注PCE数据、非农就业报告和12月FOMC会议。Privorotsky认为，真正可能迫使美联储重新评估政策路径的是11月CPI数据，但这一数据距离当前仍有一段时间。 值得注意的是，高盛经济学家目前仍预计美联储将在12月加息25个基点，并于2027年3月再次加息，而债券市场定价与这一预测存在明显分歧。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 宁可买楼，也不投AI：拼多多为什么不怕被颠覆？
articles.summary: 拼多多交出了一份收入几乎零增长的财报，财报当晚股价却逆势暴涨11%。国内电商业务重新加速、Temu收缩投入、利润率显著改善，让市场重新审视这家公司的盈利能力。 更有意思的是，当互联网巨头纷纷投入巨资争夺AI时代的入口时，手握4554亿元现金的拼多多却宁愿买楼，也没有加入算力军备竞赛。AI可能重塑电商行业，但拼多多或许有充分的理由保持冷静。 01 收入零增长，华尔街为什么奖励了11%？ 11月19日，拼多多交出了一份颇为矛盾的财报：第三季度收入1083亿元，同比增长仅0.1%，比市场预期低约6%。按照互联网行业惯常的估值逻辑，收入增长突然停滞通常不是什么好消息。然而，拼多多当晚美股却逆势大涨约11%，与同期承压的科技股形成鲜明对照。 华尔街显然看到了另一组数字。拼多多第三季度Non-GAAP营业利润达到326亿元，同比增长20.5%，超出市场预期16.4%；营业利润率由上年同期的25%提升至30.1%。更重要的是，公司在线营销收入达到598亿元，同比增长12.1%，大幅超出市场此前约6%的增长预期。 这份财报释放了两个信号：拼多多的国内基本盘可能远比市场想象中稳固，而此前不断压制盈利的投入压力，已经开始出现缓解。 国内电商，可能比想象中更好 过去一年，拼多多在线营销收入增速经历了一轮明显下滑，从2025年一季度的14.8%，逐步降至2026年一季度的2.5%，二季度也只有3.5%。这很容易让投资者产生一种印象：国内消费疲弱，淘宝、京东、抖音又在争夺低价商品市场，拼多多的增长优势正在消失。 ……

articles.title: 高盛交易员“重拾2018年剧本”：至今清晰记得“12月24日那天，客户问为什么跌这么多？我完全不知道”
articles.summary: 美股连续七日下跌，高盛衍生品交易员警告，当前市场正显现2018年四季度暴跌行情的相似特征，本轮调整可能尚未结束。 高盛衍生品策略师Brian Garrett在周五发布的报告中指出，当 前市场走势、技术面和交易结构均与2018年有明显相似之处。他通过对比两轮行情的指数跌幅，评估主要股指可能面临的进一步调整空间。 Garrett回忆起2018年12月24日的市场崩跌。 当时，一位客户问他：“为什么今天跌了这么多？”Garrett坦言：“完全不知道。” 即便是经验丰富的交易员，面对突如其来的剧烈抛售，也难以判断市场究竟为何失控。 不过，历史相似并不意味着行情必然重复。此次市场调整中，信用市场尚未出现明显恶化，美联储也没有释放政策转向信号。高盛认为，这些差异可能成为判断本轮调整是否接近尾声的关键。 2018年行情再现？高盛警告美股调整或远未结束 2018年四季度，美股在美联储持续加息、技术面破位和系统性抛售压力叠加下大幅下跌，标普500指数从高点回落近20%，并在圣诞节前夕触底。 高盛将当前主要股指自10月6日高点以来的跌幅，与2018年同期走势进行对比。 截至周四收盘，标普500已走完2018年同期跌幅的42%，纳斯达克100为69%，罗素2000则仅为24%。 如果将2018年剩余跌幅映射至当前行情，高盛模型显示，主要股指仍可能面临进一步调整。其中，标普500尚未走完当年同期的跌幅，意味着下行风险仍未充分释放。 时间维度上，2018年标普500从阶段高点到最终触底历时65个交易日。截至周五，本轮调整已持续约33个交易日。若沿着相似节奏演进，市场底部可能要等到明年1月第一个完整交易周才会出现。 信用市场反应滞后，美联储尚未释放转向信号 与2018年相比，当前信用市场的压力明显较轻。高盛数据显示，投资级信用利差自近期高点以来仅走阔5个基点，高收益债利差走阔38个基点，均明显低于2018年同期的变化幅度。 利率市场也没有出现同等程度的避险反应。 当前10年期掉期利率较近期高点下行23个基点，而短端利率变化更小。这表明，市场尚未像2018年那样，对经济和政策前景进行全面重新定价。 2018年市场反转的重要催化剂，是时任美联储主席鲍威尔在次年1月4日释放“保持耐心”的信号。 而当前，高盛经济学家仍预计美联储明年3月再次加息，政策预期尚未转向宽松。巴克莱也指出，投资者目前看不到美联储出手托底的可能性。 避险资产失灵，恐慌情绪与市场分化加剧 传统避险资产并未在本轮调整中发挥应有作用。自近期高点以来，黄金下跌10.8%，日元兑美元走弱约1%；而在2018年同期，黄金上涨5%，日元则升值2.1%。避险资产表现与历史行情明显背离。 市场恐慌程度持续升高。 高盛波动率团队在报告中将当前市场恐慌程度评为9分（满分10分），VIX指数升至30.3，距离2018年圣诞节前夕的36.1峰值已不远，但当前标普500的累计跌幅还不到2018年同期的一半。 交易结构也在放大市场波动。高盛估算，做市商目前持有约10亿美元净空Gamma头寸，可能在市场下跌时加剧对冲卖盘。客户近期开始卖出高溢价尾部期权，反映出市场参与者正调整对波动率的交易策略。 个股和投资组合表现同样出现明显分化。英伟达自10月初以来累计下跌约39%，承受较大的抛售压力。高盛追踪的2258个投资篮子中，上半年表现较好的组合在下半年普遍回撤；上半年涨幅超过一倍的篮子，下半年回报中位数约为-50%。此前的领涨交易正遭遇集中出清。 反弹可能只是喘息，市场底部仍待确认 市场并非没有短期反弹的条件。仓位已经明显出清，恐慌指标接近极值，部分客户开始卖出波动率，纳斯达克100也接近超卖区域。此外，历史上标普500跌破200日均线后曾出现短期反弹，假期缩短交易周也可能为市场带来喘息。 但短期反弹信号并不意味着市场已经筑底。 2018年行情真正反转前，信用利差明显走阔，美联储也释放了政策立场转变的信号；而这两个关键条件目前都尚未出现。 Garrett认为，在信用市场出现明显恶化，或美联储政策立场发生变化之前，市场反弹可能只是“租来的”。投资者仍需等待信用风险和货币政策给出更明确的信号，才能判断本轮调整是否真正接近尾声。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 孙正义的万亿美元豪赌：曾考虑收购SK海力士
articles.summary: 软银创始人孙正义的AI扩张野心，再度瞄准全球存储芯片巨头。 据The Information近日报道援引知情人士， 孙正义近期曾就收购韩国SK海力士一事接触华尔街机构，探讨融资可能性，交易规模或高达1万亿美元。不过，软银随后确认曾探讨这一方案，但表示目前已不再积极推进。 软银发言人称：“软银会探索许多机会，这一项目目前已不在积极考虑之列。” 若这项收购计划最终落地，软银原本有望直接切入全球存储芯片市场，进一步扩大在AI供应链中的影响力。但近万亿美元的交易规模，加上融资和监管障碍，使这一构想难以推进。 尽管收购计划已暂时搁置，孙正义对AI基础设施的布局野心仍值得关注。随着存储芯片成为AI算力扩张的关键资源，SK海力士恰好补上了软银现有产业版图中相对缺失的一环。 此次收购构想也由此折射出软银进一步向AI产业链核心环节延伸的意图。 近万亿美元交易，融资与监管双重受阻 SK海力士今年7月在美国完成上市，目前市值约5800亿美元。若按照此前较高市值给予约40%的并购溢价，交易总价值将接近1万亿美元。 融资是这笔交易面临的首要难题。软银此前已大举投资OpenAI，并以Arm股份作为抵押，为其646亿美元的投资提供资金支持。The Information指出， 目前没有迹象表明华尔街机构愿意为这笔潜在收购提供所需规模的融资。 孙正义过去多次通过股权质押和资产处置为大型投资筹资。他曾以软银持有的阿里巴巴股份作为抵押并逐步减持，为包括320亿美元收购Arm在内的交易提供资金。2017年，他还联合沙特和阿联酋主权财富基金，发起规模达1000亿美元的软银愿景基金，投资Uber、字节跳动和WeWork等企业。 融资之外，监管障碍同样突出。韩国对外资收购本国核心科技资产设有严格限制，SK海力士作为韩国重要的半导体企业，由日本软银主导收购能否获得政府批准存在重大疑问。 此外，目前也没有迹象表明控制SK海力士的韩国SK集团有意出售。 存储芯片成为软银AI版图的关键拼图 孙正义瞄准SK海力士，背后有明确的产业逻辑。该公司是全球高带宽内存（HBM）市场的主要供应商，其产品是英伟达等厂商制造高端AI芯片的重要组件，与三星电子、美光科技共同主导这一市场。 今年上半年，HBM需求旺盛推动大型存储厂商利润率接近80%，相关公司股价一度翻倍。 随着AI算力需求持续增长，存储芯片在AI基础设施中的战略地位进一步提升。 目前，软银已布局AI产业链的多个关键环节，包括持有芯片IP公司Arm的多数股权，旗下拥有数据中心与能源公司SB Energy、芯片设计公司Ampere和数据中心融资机构DigitalBridge，同时持有英特尔和OpenAI的重要股份。 相比之下，存储芯片仍是软银AI版图中相对缺失的一环。 若能收购SK海力士，软银将进一步打通从芯片设计、算力基础设施到存储供应链的布局。这也解释了孙正义为何将目光投向这家韩国芯片巨头。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 2.3万亿美元“灰飞烟灭”！美国芯片股上一次跌这么惨，还是2001年，英伟达已经“跌掉一个亚马逊”
articles.summary: AI交易的三大支柱同时松动，美国科技股遭遇猛烈抛售，市场对AI泡沫和经济增长放缓的担忧迅速升温。 本周， 费城半导体指数（SOX）重挫逾10%，创2001年以来最惨烈的单周表现，芯片板块整体市值蒸发约2.3万亿美元。英伟达股价连续第七周下跌，创2008年以来最长连跌纪录，自历史高点以来市值缩水约2.7万亿美元，相当于跌掉一个亚马逊。 抛售潮迅速蔓延至整个美股市场。标普500指数连续七个交易日下跌，单周跌幅超过9%，创近年来最大单周跌幅；纳斯达克100指数单周下跌逾10%，年内涨幅悉数回吐。VIX一度突破40，市场恐慌情绪急剧升温。 值得注意的是，英伟达财报表现亮眼、Anthropic创纪录IPO相继登场，却都未能提振市场信心。AI巨头融资态度转变、IPO抽走市场流动性，加上美联储鹰派立场不变，令市场开始重新审视这轮AI行情的支撑基础。 芯片股遭遇2001年以来最惨单周抛售，英伟达跌掉一个亚马逊 本周，费城半导体指数下跌逾10%，芯片板块市值蒸发约2.3万亿美元，创2001年以来最惨烈的单周表现。 英伟达同样未能幸免。尽管公司最新季度业绩和业绩指引均超出市场预期，股价仍连续七周下跌，创2008年以来最长连跌纪录。 周五股价进一步大跌，收于2025年5月以来最低水平。 从10月历史高点以来，英伟达股价累计下跌约47%，市值缩水约2.7万亿美元，相当于一个亚马逊。 目前公司市值约3.03万亿美元，已低于Alphabet。 值得注意的是，英伟达基本面并未明显转弱：公司连续第17个季度超越卖方预期，第四季度营收指引达到1300亿美元，高于市场预期的1250亿美元，还将2028财年增长预期从70%上调至75%。 市场担忧的焦点，正在转向AI生态系统的融资和增长模式。 英伟达收缩“AI央行”角色，生态系统融资支持转向审慎 据MarketWatch报道，英伟达新任董事长Harvey Jones明确表示，黄仁勋不会回归公司，同时释放出收紧客户融资支持的信号：只有在项目具备土地、电力和建筑等实体条件后，公司才会提供担保支持。 高盛TMT团队将此解读为英伟达正在主动收缩“AI央行”角色。此前，英伟达不仅是芯片供应商，也通过融资担保等方式支持AI生态系统。 如今态度转向审慎，可能冲击依赖英伟达担保或承购支持的纯新云计算公司。 Citadel Securities的Nohshad Shah指出，像黄仁勋这样的创始人能够推动公司承担职业经理人难以向董事会交代的高风险投资。 高盛Rich Privorotsky则认为，英伟达此前被视为AI生态系统的“多头看跌期权”，如今这一角色已经逆转，甚至成为市场的“空头看跌期权”。 Anthropic创纪录IPO反成流动性黑洞，AI资产遭遇集中抛售 Anthropic原本被视为AI产业信心的又一次验证。这家Claude开发商以高于发行区间的价格定价，融资规模达1073亿美元（含向芯片和云供应商的260亿美元配售），完全稀释估值约1.5万亿美元。 但IPO未能提振市场，反而引发流动性冲击。Anthropic股价以111.50美元开盘，随后迅速遭到抛售。纳斯达克100指数从盘前上涨2%转为下跌2%，AI股票篮子也从上涨4%转为下跌2%，标普500指数当日市值蒸发约1.3万亿美元。 市场人士认为， 投资者为参与IPO提前筹集资金，加剧了其他资产的抛售。 黄金、加密货币、铜和英伟达股票均在IPO前数日遭到卖出。彭博援引分析指出，比特币在发行前的异常下跌，与投资者筹集认购资金的行为相符。 至周五收盘，Anthropic股价跌至83.10美元附近，几乎回到83美元的发行价，较周四115.10美元的高点下跌逾25%。 承销商已全额行使超额配售权，额外出售1.47亿股，意味着稳定股价的潜在工具进一步减少。 美联储鹰派施压，市场脆弱结构放大跌势 美联储本周进一步强化紧缩信号。理事Waller重申支持加息50个基点的立场，指出约70%的核心服务项目涨幅仍超过3%，美联储可能需要收回去年全部三次预防性降息，甚至采取更多行动。 他还表示，可能需要通过政策行动“震慑市场”。 10月会议纪要也显示，部分官员曾倾向于加息，许多与会者认为AI需求持续对供给形成压力并推高价格。 彭博数据显示，美联储官员鹰鸽表态指标已升至2023年以来最鹰派水平。 市场结构则进一步放大了抛售。据高盛Prime数据，基本面多空净杠杆本月再下降7.6个百分点，降至五年多来最低水平。做市商在周五期权到期前持有大量空头伽马头寸，使下跌更容易触发进一步对冲卖盘。 高盛数据显示，周三标普500期货盘口深度平均仅为420万美元，是过去四年来流动性最差的交易日之一。不过，资金并未全面撤离：截至11月18日当周，全球股票基金净流入592亿美元，科技基金净流入123亿美元，显示部分投资者仍在逢低买入。 债市转向增长担忧，AI交易面临重新定价 与股市同步下跌的还有美债收益率。 尽管美联储官员持续释放鹰派信号，10年期美债收益率仍连续五个交易日下行，从5.17%降至4.90%，结束了自2007年以来最长的持续高于5%的时期。 高盛Rich Privorotsky认为，长端收益率可能已经开始反映政策失误的风险。收益率下行的同时，盈亏平衡通胀率也在收缩，这一组合表明市场关注点正从通胀转向经济增长和流动性。 换言之，市场担忧正在发生变化：投资者不再只关注通胀顽固和高利率，也开始担心紧缩政策可能过度，以及AI投资热潮能否持续支撑经济增长。 Baird董事总经理Ted Mortonson表示，2026年上半年的市场充斥着过度亢奋、投机和自满，而本月以来市场情绪已经转向恐惧与恐慌。 Privorotsky的判断则更为谨慎：在央行政策真正转向之前，市场反弹仍可能是卖出机会。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: “抛售“带来“更多抛售”！高盛预测“未来一周美股将出现另一波大规模抛售”
articles.summary: 美股新一轮剧烈抛售正在蔓延，高盛警告，市场可能陷入“抛售引发更多抛售”的恶性循环，未来一周仍有大规模卖盘等待释放。 11月21日，据彭博报道，高盛交易员周五发布研报称， 该行“恐慌指数”已升至10分满分中的9分，系统性投资者的抛售压力全面扩散。根据高盛模型，即使市场保持平稳，趋势追踪基金未来一周仍可能抛售数百亿美元股票；若市场进一步下跌，卖盘规模还将显著扩大。 本轮跌势已对科技股造成沉重打击。纳斯达克100指数周五单日重挫5.6%，创2020年3月以来最大单周跌幅；费城半导体指数大跌11%，英伟达自10月6日高点以来累计下挫近50%。与此同时，抛售开始波及散户偏好股票及加密货币相关资产，市场压力正从机构持仓向更广泛的风险资产扩散。 更令市场担忧的是，原本被寄予厚望的Anthropic IPO未能成为提振风险偏好的催化剂，而AI基础设施投资回报的疑虑仍在压制科技股估值。多重压力叠加之下，市场尚未出现明确的企稳信号。 系统性卖盘仍有释放空间，未来一周或再抛售806亿美元 高盛估算，以商品交易顾问（CTA）为代表的趋势追踪策略过去一个月已抛售570亿美元股票，其美股净头寸已转为净空仓190亿美元。 但机构减仓可能远未结束。 高盛模型预测，未来一周，若市场维持平盘，CTA仍可能卖出658亿美元股票；若市场继续下跌，潜在卖出规模将达到806亿美元；即便股市反弹，也可能触发286亿美元卖盘。 这类策略根据市场价格走势和波动率机械调整仓位，市场下跌会进一步触发减仓，形成“越跌越卖”的负反馈。高盛的测算意味着，趋势追踪基金仍可能成为短期市场的重要卖压来源，甚至在股市反弹时也未必停止抛售。 IPO提振预期落空，AI回报疑虑加剧市场抛售 市场此前期待Anthropic IPO成为推动资金重返风险资产的转折点，但这一预期最终落空。高盛交易员指出，不少投资者原本希望这笔大型科技IPO能够提振市场情绪，推动年末资金重新流入风险资产，但其对整体市场的带动作用有限。 高盛交易员将这一结果形容为“难以下咽的苦果”。 与此同时，投资者对AI巨额资本开支能否兑现回报的质疑持续升温。市场开始重新审视AI芯片、算力及基础设施投入能否产生足够收益，以支撑科技股当前估值。英伟达周五单日下跌14%，自10月高点以来跌幅接近50%，成为本轮科技股调整的主要拖累因素。 抛售压力也已扩散至散户投资者。高盛追踪的散户偏好股票组合周五下跌8.9%。此外， 高盛周期股相对防御股的比较篮子下跌3.2%，显示资金正在从周期性板块转向防御性资产。 从CTA持续减仓到散户投机性资产遭到抛售，市场去风险正在进一步扩散。若科技股持续承压并触发更多趋势策略减仓，美股可能面临新一轮抛售压力。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
